name: Documentary Research Overlay Timelapse
use_when: A documentary or explainer needs to show research, investigation, editing, browsing, document review, practice, or discovery.
Raw screen recording would feel flat, slow, or too literal.
Documents, screenshots, or search results can be layered over a process recording to make the research feel active.
avoid_when: The documents contain private, sensitive, or uncleared information.
The overlays imply evidence that the narration has not actually verified.
The speed-up makes the source context impossible to understand when context matters.

timeline_pattern.pattern: record_process -> choose_documents_or_screens -> overlay_above_process -> blend_or_key_background -> optional_speedup -> riser_or_tension_bed -> hold_context_frame -> transition_to_claim
timeline_pattern.process_rule: Record the real process when possible: researching, editing, practicing, collecting sources, or reviewing evidence.
timeline_pattern.overlay_rule: Layer documents or screenshots only when they support the current story beat.
timeline_pattern.speed_rule: Use speed-up for energy, but pause or hold on any frame that must function as evidence.
timeline_pattern.context_rule: End the sequence with enough context for the viewer to understand what the research discovered.

motion.rule: Make research feel active with layered documents, blend modes, and time compression while preserving source context.

keyframe_values.timelapse: Speed up process footage only until motion feels active; reduce speed or add holds when text must be read.
keyframe_values.overlay_opacity: Use blend/opacity only as far as needed to remove flat backgrounds without losing document text.
keyframe_values.hold_frame: Hold the final proof or discovery frame long enough for a first-time viewer to understand the takeaway.

sound.rule: A restrained riser or low anticipation bed can add intrigue during the research build, but it must stay below narration and resolve before the next spoken claim.

captions.rule: Captions should avoid layered documents and should be simplified or suppressed if the screen text is the primary reading path.

color.rule: Do not grade or blend research overlays so heavily that source text, UI, or privacy redactions become unclear.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use setpts for speed-up, overlay and blend filters for documents/screens, opacity fades for entrances, and audio fades for a riser or tension bed.
implementation.remotion: Build a ResearchOverlayTimelapse component with processVideo, overlayAssets, blendMode, speedMultiplier, holdFrames, redactionRegions, and sfxCue frames.
implementation.blender: Use video planes for process footage and document planes with alpha/blend materials; animate opacity and camera/crop for focus.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Record the process, place documents or screen captures above it, choose a blend mode that removes unwanted background, speed up the section when appropriate, then add a restrained riser.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use nested screen recordings, document overlays with blend modes/opacity, Speed/Duration or time remapping, and a low riser on a separate audio track.

common_mistakes: Using fake or unrelated research visuals as wallpaper.
Showing private tabs, emails, account names, or source details without redaction.
Speeding the sequence until no evidence can be inspected.
Letting overlays and captions compete for the same text-reading area.
Adding a loud riser that makes the section feel like a trailer instead of research.
qc: Does every visible document or screen support the claim being made?
Are private, sensitive, or uncleared details removed or approved?
Can the viewer understand the research takeaway before the sequence exits?
Do captions avoid the document or UI text being inspected?
Does the riser stay below narration and resolve cleanly into the next beat?
